provenance.cannot_be_recomputed: The paper's 18/21 resistance and 12/16 endurance validation accuracy. Scoring needs a predicted and a measured direction per measurement; SupplementTableS1.xlsx names the 9 validation papers and records neither. Quoted in the paper's Figure 3 and nowhere recomputable from the archive.
provenance.fitted_to: Human and rodent skeletal muscle, validated on humans. The network is built from '87 published studies of human or rodent skeletal muscle cell responses to endurance or resistance exercise in vivo or simulated exercise in vitro' (their abstract). The validation set is nine published papers and, in their words, 'the validation studies included data from 140 human subjects of both sexes'; they score themselves 18/21 (85%) on resistance and 12/16 (75%) on endurance against it (their Figure 3). Of the three models this project runs it is the only one validated on humans at all -- the fibre's is fitted to mouse fast-twitch fibres and the cell's to biosensor recordings. Which human muscle a bout is shown under is still OURS: the paper models a resistance bout and an endurance bout and names no muscle.

provenance.integrator: SciPy odeint on the ported right-hand side. The authors integrate the same equations from the same table in their notebook; the port is ours and its nine contract items are listed in fowler/model.py.
provenance.known_discrepancy: Stored notebook cells 22 and 47, the endurance arm, reproduce only 29/121 and 21/121 and the cause is unidentified — 121 single-node knockdown sweeps and six alternate protocols did not recover them. The substituted spreadsheet reproduces Figure 4B exactly, so the corruption is in the archived notebook session and not in the network table these scenarios run.
provenance.model_version: 121 species / 261 reaction rows, of which 259 are interactions once the two exercise-input rows and the two duplicate rules are removed — the paper's own count for the interactions. THEIR ABSTRACT SAYS 120 NODES against this table's 121: receptors (8), target genes (28) and phenotypes (12) agree exactly, and their 14 transcriptional regulators are 15 here. One node is unaccounted for, and it is left standing rather than rounded away — 121 is what the shipped table holds and what runs. Normalised-Hill ODEs, the authors' default weights, n and EC50 from SupplementTableS3.xlsx unmodified.
provenance.uncertainty: NO BAND SHIPS AND THE AUTHORS DRAW NONE. What they publish is a perturbation: 'when n_H and EC50 were increased from 1.4 and 0.5 to 2.0 and 0.6, validation accuracy decreased from 81% to 76% for resistance and from 75% to 69% for endurance. When n_H and EC50 were decreased to 1.0 and 0.4, accuracy decreased to 62% for resistance and 50% for endurance. Hence the model results were quite robust.' Their accuracy score cannot be recomputed here (see cannot_be_recomputed), but the perturbation itself runs: every reaction row in this network carries n = 1.4 and EC50 = 0.5, so their setting is a global rewrite of two numbers. Measured on this protocol (validation/fowler_parameter_uncertainty.py): at their INCREASED setting 88 of 121 nodes end the bout more than 0.05 away from where they end here, median 0.1395, worst 0.6033 (Anti_Inflammatory); at their DECREASED setting 70 of 121 move more than 0.05, median 0.0593, worst 0.2434 (LATS1_2). 0.05 is the threshold this app uses to call the two arms different. The twelve drawn outputs' widest gap is 0.0383 here, 0.0505 under their increase and 0.0138 under their decrease -- the gap moves further than the gap. Read the single line as one setting of two parameters, not as a prediction with a range around it.
provenance.validation: 23,738 of 23,980 published doubles reproduce. Figure 4A 7,744/7,744 (worst 5.24e-08), 4B 8,008/8,008 (2.13e-08), 4C 7,744/7,744 (5.32e-08); stored notebook cells 21 and 45 reproduce 121/121 at 6.1e-13 and 1.0e-11. Not one published number is wrong — 34 of the row/column LABELS are, and the corrected map is in validation/fowler_compare.py.
provenance.what_the_authors_also_ran: This run is the authors' 45 minutes and stops there. Theirs does not: Figure 2 is 'model-predicted changes in phenotypes relative to baseline during 45 min of exercise AND 15 H RECOVERY', over which they report the phenotypes returning toward baseline while 'a significant number of genes remained significantly upregulated after 15 h of rest' and 'by 15 h the differences in muscle phenotypes between exercise modality were negligible'. Their Figure 5 also runs the two bouts back to back, 45 min of resistance followed immediately by 45 min of endurance and the reverse, against 90 min of each alone. None of that is run here. Note the inversion while descending: the fibre scale shows a recovery segment that is OURS (no published Francis run holds one) and this scale, where the authors published one, shows none.
